# What's new in Search Console

Google presented five Search Console launches. Query groups cluster queries with the same intent (computed with AI, shown in Insights, with no effect on ranking). An AI-powered configuration turns a natural-language request into Performance report filters and applies them only after the user approves. The generative AI control lets owners decide whether content may be used in AI results, and a generative AI report counts impressions in AI surfaces by page, country and device, while the regular Performance report still includes AI traffic. Platform properties let owners verify Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube accounts through a pop-up from the platform and see the traffic Google Search, Discover and News send to them. Multimodal search reporting, announced on 24 September 2026, covers Lens, Circle to Search and image searches. The generative AI control and report repeat Day 1, where Google's launch post dated the report 3 June 2026, rolled out to all sites by 31 August 2026. Query groups (announced 27 October 2025) are available only to properties with a large volume of queries, the AI-powered configuration is experimental and visible to a small percentage of users with 20 requests a day, and a claimed Search profile adds its verified accounts as platform properties automatically. Day 1 and Day 2 added existing tools to that picture: Google points to the Crawl Stats report (Settings, Crawl stats) as the most valuable tool for debugging crawl errors alongside server logs, showing how much Google crawls, the errors it received, the content types fetched and the split between discovery and refresh crawling, and Google's site move guide and a community migration both use the Change of Address tool. In the Day 1 Q&A John Mueller said that if Crawl Stats shows about half of a site's crawling going to discovering new pages, crawling of new pages is not the problem, and Google said soft 404s are looked up in the page indexing report rather than in Crawl Stats. An audio recording of Day 1's robots.txt talk added the robots.txt report: it shows the file as Google last fetched it, with a version history and the errors and successes of each fetch, and Google said it uses Google's open-source parser and helps catch CDNs that change robots.txt without the owner knowing and hosts that cloak the file (the last two points are not in Google's docs). A community speaker said publishers can verify their social accounts in Search Console to track repurposed content, which fits the platform properties launched on Day 3.

## What to do

- Review the filters and regexes the AI-powered configuration proposes before relying on the numbers.
- Add each social or video account as a platform property and compare formats by URL pattern, such as /watch against /shorts/.
- Select the multimodal search type to see image-led searches, and expect no query dimension there.
- Check the version history in the robots.txt report after CDN or hosting changes.

  <br><sub>`D3-C450` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Platform properties roll out globally, plus a new social and video performance guide](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/07/platform-properties-social-video-guide), [Analyze your social and video platform content performance in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/analyze-social-video-content)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a YouTube platform property, long-form and short-form videos can be compared in the Performance report's comparison mode by URL pattern, /watch versus /shorts/; Instagram posts (/p/) and reels can be compared the same way.
  <br><sub>`D3-C451` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Analyze your social and video platform content performance in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/analyze-social-video-content) · Used by `DEV-MON-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** In the example YouTube report shown in Google's Search Console talk, long-form videos still got more traffic and more impressions from Google than Shorts; this was one example channel, not a general finding.
  <br><sub>`D3-C452` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Search Console talk presented multimodal search reporting as its fifth and newest launch, under a 'Hot from the oven' badge.
  > "5. Multimodal search reporting"
  <br><sub>`D3-C454` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Multimodal search reporting in Search Console launched about a week and a half before the 2 October 2026 talk.
  <br><sub>`D3-C455` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Until the multimodal launch, the Search Console Performance report essentially showed only text-based searches.
  <br><sub>`D3-C457` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc), [Performance report (Search results): Overview and basic setup](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Multimodal searches reported in Search Console include searches with Google Lens, Circle to Search on Android, images uploaded to Google Search and Chrome's right-click search on an image.
  <br><sub>`D3-C458` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc), [Performance report (Search results): Overview and basic setup](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Multimodal search type*</sub>

- **[Stage]** To see multimodal traffic in the Search Console Performance report, select the multimodal search type instead of the default text-based one.
  <br><sub>`D3-C459` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc), [Performance report (Search results): Overview and basic setup](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Multimodal search type*</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a demo, asking Chrome about an image on a web page opened a side panel of visual matches, one of which was on Google's developers site and led on to more information about Search Console; Google described this as the full flow of the multimodal traffic now reported.
  <br><sub>`D3-C461` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Search with Google Lens in Chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/15086890?hl=en), [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's site move guide says to submit a Change of Address in Search Console when moving from one domain or subdomain to another, to submit the new sitemap, and to change internal links on the new site from the old URLs to the new ones.
  <br><sub>`D2-C912` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`, the glossary term *Change of Address tool*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's query groups announcement (27 October 2025) says the groups are computed with AI, may change over time and do not affect ranking, and that query groups are available only to properties with a large volume of queries.
  <br><sub>`D3-C463` · Search Central blog (27 October 2025) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups) · Used by the glossary term *Query groups*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Search Console help says the experimental AI-powered configuration is visible only to a small percentage of users, allows each user 20 requests per day, keeps existing report filters when it adds new ones, and applies its suggested settings only after the user confirms them.
  <br><sub>`D3-C464` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/17011165?hl=en) · Used by the glossary term *AI-powered configuration*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's announcement of 24 September 2026 says multimodal search data appears both in the Performance report for Search results and in the generative AI performance report, can be exported, and began rolling out globally that day.
  <br><sub>`D3-C465` · Search Central blog (24 September 2026) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Generative AI performance report*, the glossary term *Multimodal search type*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's help page on platform properties says ownership is checked periodically and, if the external login expires, access pauses until the account is re-verified; each account or channel needs its own property, and data takes a few days to appear.
  <br><sub>`D3-C466` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [About platform properties in Search Console](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/17148418?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-09`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's help page says platform properties show only how content performs on Google Search, Discover and Google News, not how often it is seen on the social or video platform itself.
  <br><sub>`D3-C467` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [About platform properties in Search Console](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/17148418?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-09`, the glossary term *Platform properties*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's social and video performance guide says that if you already claimed your Search profile, all of its verified accounts are added automatically as platform properties in Search Console.
  <br><sub>`D3-C468` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [Analyze your social and video platform content performance in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/analyze-social-video-content) · Extends [D1-C025](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Extends [D2-C960](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S14-lightning-session-f-media.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-09`, the glossary term *Search profile*</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** The Google archive page cited on the Britney Spears slide lists 593 spellings (the correct one plus 592 misspellings), each typed by at least two different users within a three-month period and corrected by Google's spelling system; it is an old jobs page (footer 2011), so the figures are historical.
  <br><sub>`D3-C416` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The speaker placed the query groups launch, hedging, in December, but Google's announcement is dated 27 October 2025 with a gradual rollout over the following weeks, so many sites may first have seen the card around December 2025.
  <br><sub>`D3-C426` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For content planning, read query groups (and their trending up and trending down views) as intent themes: write for the intent the group stands for, not for each spelling or phrasing variant in it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C427` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Review the filters and regexes that Search Console's AI-powered configuration proposes before trusting the numbers: Google's launch post calls the feature experimental, warns that AI can misinterpret requests, and limits it to the Search results Performance report (not Discover or News) and to configuration, not sorting or exporting.
  <br><sub>`D3-C435` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · Repeats [D1-C243](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) · Extended by [D3-C501](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Search Console's generative AI performance reports count impressions only, with no clicks and no query dimension (Google documents the Search report for AI Overviews and AI Mode, plus a separate Discover report), so measure visits that follow AI answers with your own analytics.
  <br><sub>`D3-C441` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Media teams that publish on YouTube, Instagram, TikTok or X should add each account as a Search Console platform property and compare formats by URL pattern; Google's July 2026 post says an account already used for a Search profile should already give access to its data.
  <br><sub>`D3-C453` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's Performance report help says the queries dimension is not available for the multimodal search type, because these searches mostly use images, so judge image-led traffic by page, country and device, and make product and article images distinctive enough for Lens to match.
  <br><sub>`D3-C462` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-CAN-09`: Keep migration redirects in place long term and judge a move in Search Console, not with site: queries
- Requirement `DEV-MON-04`: Monitor Crawl stats and server logs for verified Googlebot traffic
- Requirement `DEV-MON-07`: Track AI feature visibility in the Generative AI performance report
- Requirement `DEV-MON-09`: Add the brand's YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and X accounts to Search Console as platform properties
- Requirement `DEV-MON-11`: Measure the time from publishing a URL to Googlebot's first crawl of it
- Requirement `DEV-SRV-05`: Rely only on the fields Google supports (user-agent, allow, disallow, sitemap) and keep robots.txt under 500 KiB
- Requirement `DEV-SRV-06`: Do not put Content-Signal or other non-standard lines between user-agent lines
